purpose: Establish a reproducible natural-language reference on three difficulty levels before designing or comparing alternative communication protocols.
research_question: What progress, message traffic, and inference cost does the pinned local model achieve under CRAFT's natural-language communication setup across simple, medium, and complex hidden-information structures?

adapter: Seed and sample D1, D2, D3 without replacement: exactly one message call per role per turn.
All Directors observe the same pre-round conversation; the Builder receives all three extracted messages.
Parser extracts the message region, removes one outer square-bracket envelope and formatting tags, and otherwise preserves the generated prose exactly.
Child process console encoding is UTF-8.

model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; 99 GPU layers; one slot; context 4096; logical batch 1024; physical micro-batch 256; Director temperature 0.7/max_tokens 500; Builder temperature 0.1/max_tokens 250

design.communication_condition: pinned CRAFT natural-language speaker prompts and extracted public messages
design.pairing: Reference task manifest for any later format study; no alternative condition is included here.

primary: final progress and completion per structure
generated, parsed, and Builder-delivered Director messages per turn
Builder-visible transcript Qwen-token count per turn
secondary: llama.cpp prompt/generation token counts and service timing
message-format residuals after the fixed parser

analysis: Report every structure and attempted turn. Keep per-structure metrics separate and give their unweighted mean only as a descriptive summary. Include errors and truncation. Do not claim superiority or statistical significance. A later comparison must reuse the same structures, role schedule, parser, model/runtime, move oracle, and turn limit, with its own preregistration.
